The vibration damping device includes a tubular outer attachment member and an inner attachment member disposed relative to the outer attachment member. The outer attachment member and the inner attachment member are elastically connected to one another by a pair of main rubber portions. These main rubber portions are arranged so as to be spaced apart from each other in the axial direction of the device, thereby defining a liquid chamber between them.

A partition portion is also provided between the outer attachment member and the inner attachment member. The partition portion couples the outer attachment member to the inner attachment member and divides the liquid chamber into a first liquid chamber and a second liquid chamber. In this configuration, vibration input to the device can cause liquid to move between the first and second liquid chambers, thereby producing a damping effect.

The partition portion includes an annular rigid portion. The annular rigid portion is provided with a restricted passage that connects the first liquid chamber and the second liquid chamber. The restricted passage limits and controls the flow of liquid between the two chambers, so that damping performance can be obtained based on the flow resistance of the liquid passing through the restricted passage.

The partition portion further includes an annular elastic portion. The annular elastic portion is arranged in a radially compressed state and is held in contact with the annular rigid portion. However, the annular elastic portion is not bonded to the annular rigid portion. As a result, the annular elastic portion can maintain contact with the rigid portion while allowing relative behavior between the elastic portion and the rigid portion, which may improve assembly flexibility and contribute to the vibration damping characteristics of the device.

A vibration damping device includes a tubular outer attachment member and an inner attachment member disposed inside the outer attachment member. The outer and inner attachment members are connected to each other by a plurality of main rubber elastic portions arranged at intervals in the circumferential direction. These main rubber elastic portions elastically support the inner attachment member relative to the outer attachment member and define, between adjacent rubber portions, spaces that form part of a liquid-filled chamber.

A partition member is provided between the outer attachment member and the inner attachment member so as to divide the liquid-filled chamber into two separate liquid chambers. These two liquid chambers communicate with each other through a restricted passage, such as an orifice passage. When vibration is applied between the outer and inner attachment members, the main rubber elastic portions deform, causing a pressure difference between the two liquid chambers. This pressure difference forces the sealed liquid to flow through the restricted passage. As a result, vibration energy is dissipated by the flow resistance and resonance action of the liquid, thereby producing an effective damping performance.

The partition member includes an annular rigid portion and an elastic portion. The annular rigid portion provides the partition member with the necessary shape retention and strength, while the elastic portion seals against surrounding components and accommodates deformation during operation. The elastic portion is fitted against the annular rigid portion in a radially compressed state. In particular, the elastic portion is pressed into contact with the annular rigid portion by its own elastic restoring force, without being bonded, vulcanized, or adhesively fixed to the rigid portion.

Because the elastic portion is held by radial compression rather than by bonding, the structure of the partition member can be simplified. The manufacturing process is also made easier because it is not necessary to perform a separate bonding step between the elastic material and the rigid annular member. This reduces production complexity and can improve assembly efficiency. At the same time, the compressed contact between the elastic portion and the annular rigid portion provides a reliable seal and stable positioning, allowing the liquid chambers and the restricted passage to function properly.

With this arrangement, the vibration damping device can achieve effective liquid-based damping while maintaining a simple and practical construction. The device is particularly useful in applications where vibrations must be absorbed between two members, such as in automotive mounts, suspension bushings, or other vibration-isolating supports. The combination of spaced main rubber elastic portions, divided liquid chambers, and a restricted liquid passage provides high damping capability, while the non-bonded compressed partition structure contributes to easier manufacture, improved reliability, and reduced cost.

**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may seem small and simple, but it is one of the most important words in the English language. It is called the definite article, and it helps us point to something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

“The” gives clarity to sentences. It helps identify people, places, objects, and ideas. We use it when talking about something already mentioned, something unique, or something known to everyone. For example, we say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our sky, and we say “the teacher” when we know which teacher is being discussed.

Although it is only three letters long, “the” appears everywhere in English writing and speech. It connects ideas, makes communication more precise, and gives structure to language. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or confusing.

In this way, **“the”** proves that even the smallest words can have a big impact.

A partition member is disposed between the liquid chambers and includes a restricted passage permitting fluid communication therebetween to generate vibration damping based on fluid flow.
